items.prompt: A client sends an expired Bearer token to GET /api/availability/slots and then to POST /api/appointments. What happens to each request?
items.answer: The slots list is served as usual; the booking route answers 401 UNAUTHORIZED
distractors: Both get 401, because authMiddleware rejects a bad token before any route runs
Both get 403, since a bad token maps to the lowest role
Slots return 401, and the booking is taken as a guest booking
items.explanation: authMiddleware never rejects: a failed verify just leaves req.user undefined. The slots route has no requireRole, so it runs. The booking route has requireRole(CUSTOMER), which returns 401 UNAUTHORIZED when req.user is missing.

items.prompt: A client posts a booking body with startTimeLocal missing, and validate forwards the ZodError. What does errorMiddleware send back?
distractors: A 400 response listing the Zod issues in details
A 422 with code VALIDATION_ERROR naming each bad field
400 BAD_REQUEST with no details
items.explanation: errorMiddleware only recognises AppError. Anything else, including a ZodError, is logged with console.error and answered as 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (review finding 3).

items.prompt: An anonymous visitor calls POST /api/auth/register with an otherwise valid body (email, password, names) plus role: "SYSTEM_ADMIN". What account is created?
items.answer: A SYSTEM_ADMIN account, exactly as requested
distractors: A CUSTOMER account: the role field is ignored
No account: a 403 is returned for that role
A READ_ONLY account until a manager approves it
items.explanation: The register route has no requireRole, and registerSchema accepts role as any of the six values (defaulting to CUSTOMER only when it is absent). authService.register writes it unchanged (review finding 1).

items.prompt: A customer cancels a CONFIRMED appointment that still has two PENDING reminders. When cancel returns, what state is the new APPOINTMENT_CANCELLED notification in?
items.answer: CANCELLED, like both of the reminders
distractors: PENDING, while the two reminders become CANCELLED
SENT, since the notice is sent inside the transaction
PENDING, with both reminders left PENDING too
items.explanation: cancel inserts the notice (status defaults to PENDING) inside its transaction, then after commit flips every PENDING notification for the appointment to CANCELLED, which catches the notice it just created (review finding 2).

items.prompt: A staff member is available 09:00 to 11:00 on a future day. The service lasts 30 minutes with a 10-minute buffer before and 5 after, and an appointment is already booked 09:40 to 10:10 (all times in one zone). Which slot start times does generateAvailableSlots list?
distractors: One slot, at 10:25, as buffers must clear the booking
Two slots, at 10:10 and 10:25; 09:10 touches it
items.explanation: The cursor steps every 15 minutes while 45 minutes still fit (cursors 09:00 to 10:15); each slot starts 10 minutes in and lasts 30. Overlap is tested on the un-buffered slot with the half-open rule, so 09:10-09:40 and 10:10-10:40 touch the booking without overlapping it.

items.prompt: Using the API directly, a customer makes an otherwise valid booking for Sunday at 22:00, a time covered by no availability window and no blocked window. The staff member has no other appointments. What is stored?
items.answer: A CONFIRMED appointment at 22:00 on Sunday
distractors: Nothing, since the request fails with a 409 conflict
A REQUESTED appointment that waits for staff approval
Nothing; it fails with a 400 OUTSIDE_AVAILABILITY
items.explanation: book checks the service, the staff member, a past start and overlap with other appointments. It never reads AvailabilityWindow, so the booking succeeds and is created directly as CONFIRMED (review finding 7).

items.prompt: A customer reschedules a CONFIRMED appointment, and a day later reschedules it again to a free time. What happens on the second reschedule?
items.answer: It succeeds, since the first one stored CONFIRMED, not RESCHEDULED
distractors: It fails, as RESCHEDULED may only move back to the CONFIRMED state
It fails, because one appointment may be rescheduled one time only
It succeeds, but only after a manager confirms the first change
items.explanation: reschedule checks CONFIRMED -> RESCHEDULED but then writes status CONFIRMED. The row is never stored as RESCHEDULED, so the next reschedule starts from CONFIRMED and passes the same check.

items.prompt: A scheduler creates a weekly series with count 12. Occurrences 1 to 6 are free, but occurrence 7 overlaps an existing CONFIRMED appointment. What is saved?
items.answer: Nothing: 409 RECURRENCE_CONFLICT rolls back the series row too
distractors: Six appointments and the series row, then a 409 for the rest
Eleven appointments; the conflicting week is skipped silently
All twelve appointments, with week 7 flagged as a conflict
items.explanation: createSeries runs in one transaction that first inserts the RecurrenceSeries row, then each occurrence. The first conflict throws, so the transaction rolls back everything, including the series row and the six earlier appointments.

items.prompt: A scheduler asks for a daily series with count 100 and no untilDateUtc, and every day is free. How many appointments does createSeries insert?
distractors: 100, exactly the count that was requested
None, as a count above 52 is rejected outright
53: the 52-row cap plus the first anchor
items.explanation: generateOccurrences stops at Math.min(count, maxOccurrences), and createSeries passes maxOccurrences 52. The cap applies to every frequency, not only weekly series.

items.prompt: A weekly series starts Tuesday 27 October 2026 at 09:00 in America/Chicago (14:00 UTC). US clocks fall back on 1 November. What UTC time is stored for the 3 November occurrence?
distractors: 14:00 UTC, so it reads 08:00 local
14:00 UTC, which is still 09:00 local
13:00 UTC, which reads 07:00 local
items.explanation: The cursor is a zoned Luxon DateTime and steps by weeks in local time, so every occurrence is 09:00 Chicago. After the change Chicago is UTC-6, so 09:00 local is 15:00 UTC.

items.prompt: An appointment is booked for three days from now. A manager then calls POST /api/notifications/enqueue. Which of its notifications are added to the queue?
items.answer: All three PENDING rows, the confirmation and both reminders
distractors: Only the confirmation, since both reminders lie in the future
The confirmation and the T-24h reminder, the next one due
None; enqueue picks up rows already past scheduledForUtc
items.explanation: enqueuePendingNotifications loads every PENDING notification and adds a job for each, with no scheduledForUtc filter and no jobId. Booking created three PENDING rows, so all three are queued now (review finding 8).

items.prompt: A staff member opens a CONFIRMED appointment and presses Complete. Between complete loading the row and writing it, the customer's cancel commits. What status does the appointment end with?
items.answer: COMPLETED, overwriting the cancel that committed
distractors: CANCELLED, as complete re-reads the row before writing
CANCELLED: Prisma raises P2025 and complete stops
COMPLETED, after a 409 is shown to the customer
items.explanation: complete reads the status, checks the transition, then updates where: { id } alone. With no status in the predicate the write succeeds and replaces CANCELLED (review finding 10; the canonical repo later added a compare-and-set).

items.front: Why can two concurrent bookings for the same staff member and time both succeed?
items.back: The overlap check is a plain findFirst inside a READ COMMITTED transaction, and the schema has no exclusion constraint. Both transactions can read "no conflict" and both insert. Fixes: a Postgres EXCLUDE USING gist constraint on staff and time range, or serializable isolation with retry.

items.front: What do service buffers protect against in slot generation, and what do they not protect against?
items.back: Buffers are reserved inside the availability window, so a slot keeps its distance from the window edges. The overlap test against existing appointments uses the un-buffered slot, so buffers do not keep a slot away from a neighbouring appointment.

items.front: Why does no notification ever get sent in this snapshot unless someone acts?
items.back: server.ts only starts the HTTP listener, and nothing imports the reminder or notification processors, so no BullMQ worker or sweep runs. The only trigger is a manager calling POST /api/notifications/enqueue; the recurrence processor is a placeholder.

items.front: Is RESCHEDULED a status or an event in this codebase?
items.back: The state machine treats it as a status (CONFIRMED -> RESCHEDULED -> CONFIRMED), but the service never stores it: reschedule writes CONFIRMED and records the change as an AppointmentActivity with old and new values. In practice it is an event.
